newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD appeal seen delayed further.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD appeal seen delayed further.

text.p: The Brazilian government is having a hard time gathering paperwork demanded by a judge mulling its Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) privatization appeal which will probably be further delayed, an official said.

"We're talking about tens of thousands of pages of legal documents which have to be gathered from all over Brazil. I think we'll only manage to hand them in Monday," a spokeswoman for the government's Federal Advocacy said.
The Federal Advocacy was given ten days Wednesday to provide the information by high court justice Democrito Ramos Reinaldo of the Superior Justice Tribunal who is mulling the government's appeal.
The government has asked that all lawsuits and existing injunctions involving the CVRD privatization be heard in one court, simplifying the logistics of challenging the cases.
The justice said Thursday he would examine the documents over the weekend and might have a decision by Monday.
But the spokeswoman said the process was proving difficult because 120 cases against the CVRD share auction have been lodged in courts all over Brazil.
The government's task had been made even more time-consuming because the judge demanded each document be officially recognized in public notary offices, she said.

The National Development Bank (BNDES) originally planned to auction 45 percent of CVRD's voting shares April 29, but has been forced to reschedule the sale three times because of the injunctions, two of which remain standing.
The latest date for the auction is Monday.
